description: kithd/src/transport.rs and kithd/src/discovery.rs both implement TailnetCertVerifier, which returns Ok(ServerCertVerified::assertion()) for any certificate, bypassing all X.509 validation. The rationale (Tailscale's WireGuard provides authentication at the network layer; TLS is used only for confidentiality) is documented in code comments. This design is sound under the assumption that the Tailscale network layer is not compromised, but it means: (1) Any certificate is accepted from any tailnet IP, including a self-signed cert with a wrong CN/SAN. (2) If the WireGuard layer is ever bypassed (e.g. by a Tailscale bug or misconfiguration), TLS provides no fallback authentication. The finding is P3 (informational / accepted design risk) because the security model is intentional and documented. Recommend adding a SECURITY.md section that explicitly states this trust model and its preconditions.
title: TailnetCertVerifier accepts any cert: intentional but undocumented risk
